# Acyclic SDK

Public SDK service examples and navigation for language-model consumers.

- [TypeScript guide](typescript/packages/sdk/README.md): installation, environment and execution instructions.
- [Rust guide](rust/README.md): the same six services with compiled Rust doctests.

The following complete TypeScript ES modules match the TypeScript guide and are compiled by `bun run check:docs`. Install the packages listed in that guide, set `ACYCLIC_API_KEY`, each HTTPS service `*_ENDPOINT`, and any named existing resource before running. Save a snippet as `example.mts`, compile with `npx tsc example.mts --module nodenext --target es2022 --types node`, and run `node example.mjs` on Node 22+.

## Objects

Account-scoped, content-addressed blobs: equal bytes name one blob, manifests join parts, and retained roots keep blobs alive across collection. This example publishes bytes and reads a range back over HTTP.

```ts
import { HttpObjectsV1, verified } from "@acyclic-labs/objects";

const objects = new HttpObjectsV1({ endpoint: process.env.OBJECTS_ENDPOINT!, token: process.env.ACYCLIC_API_KEY! });
const put = verified(await objects.put(new TextEncoder().encode("Hello")));
if (!put) throw new Error("outcome unknown; repeating the put is safe");
console.log((await objects.get({ digest: put.digest, range: { start: 1n }, maximumBytes: 4n })).body);
```

## Streams

Append-only record streams with forks and atomic commits. This example reads the tail position of an existing stream through the hosted HTTP provider.

```ts
import { HttpStreamProvider } from "@acyclic-labs/stream";

const streams = new HttpStreamProvider({
  endpoint: process.env.STREAM_ENDPOINT!, token: process.env.ACYCLIC_API_KEY!,
});
console.log(await streams.tail(process.env.STREAM_PATH!));
```

## Actors

Durable actor identities, invocation and subscriptions. This example inspects an existing actor using the Rust-backed client.

```ts
import { ActorsClient, ActorId } from "@acyclic-labs/actors";

const actors = new ActorsClient({
  endpoint: process.env.ACTORS_ENDPOINT!, token: process.env.ACYCLIC_API_KEY!,
});
console.log(await actors.inspectActor({
  actorId: await ActorId(process.env.ACTOR_ID!),
}));
```

## Workers

Cloud Workers are stateless Actors. This example publishes `worker.mjs` (a module exporting `default.fetch`, without an actor export), creates a deployment, invokes it and deletes it. The module is published as an Objects blob retained under its own root.

```ts
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { CodeSha256, PositiveU64 } from "@acyclic-labs/actors";
import { HttpObjectsV1 } from "@acyclic-labs/objects";
import { WorkersDeploymentClient } from "@acyclic-labs/workers";

const options = { endpoint: process.env.EDGE_ENDPOINT!, token: process.env.ACYCLIC_API_KEY! };
const workers = new WorkersDeploymentClient(options, new HttpObjectsV1(options));
const digest = await workers.publish(await readFile("worker.mjs"));
const { actor } = await workers.create({
  codeSha256: await CodeSha256(digest), homeRegion: "la", bindings: [], subscriptions: [],
  limits: { handlerTimeoutMillis: await PositiveU64(30000n), memoryBytes: await PositiveU64(268435456n), checkpointBytes: await PositiveU64(1048576n) },
  idempotencyKey: "create-worker",
});
if (!actor) throw new Error("create returned no deployment");
console.log(await workers.invoke({ actorId: actor.actorId, method: "GET", url: "/", headers: [], body: new Uint8Array() }));
await workers.delete({ actorId: actor.actorId, idempotencyKey: "delete-worker" });
```

## fs

Versioned filesystem workspaces and generations. This example opens an existing workspace through Node HTTP/2 gRPC.

```ts
import { createFilesystemGrpcClient } from "@acyclic-labs/fs/grpc";

const client = createFilesystemGrpcClient({
  endpoint: process.env.FS_ENDPOINT!, token: process.env.ACYCLIC_API_KEY!,
});
try {
  console.log(await client.filesystem.openWorkspace({
    selector: { case: "name", value: process.env.FS_WORKSPACE! },
  }));
} finally {
  client.close();
}
```

## Customer CLI

- [CLI installation and commands](plugin/README.md): Install the native executable as the `acyclic-plugin` command with `npm install -g @acyclic-labs/plugin`, or as `acyclic` with `cargo install --locked acyclic-plugin`; Cargo users link it as `acyclic-plugin` before using the commands below.
- [Identity API contract](plugin/identity-api.md): Public Edge identity requests and session refresh behavior.

Configure `ACYCLIC_API_URL` with the public Edge origin. Identity commands accept
`--endpoint ORIGIN`, `--credentials PATH`, and `--json`. The default credential
file is `~/.acyclic/identity.json`; `ACYCLIC_IDENTITY_FILE` overrides it.

`acyclic-plugin login --json` starts device approval. Relay the URL and code from stderr
to the user. Stdout contains one final JSON success or error. The user must
approve in their browser; the CLI then saves the session.

`acyclic-plugin whoami --json` returns the signed-in identity. `acyclic-plugin orgs --json`
lists organizations. These commands refresh expiring access tokens automatically.
`acyclic-plugin refresh --json` explicitly rotates the stored refresh token.
`acyclic-plugin logout --json` revokes the OAuth session and clears its local tokens,
preserving agent keys. Failed revocation retains credentials for retry.
`acyclic-plugin bearer --org ID --output NEW_FILE --json` writes a short-lived organization bearer to a new private file. Its JSON result contains only account, expiry and filename. Never read the token file into a model.
Commands exit nonzero on errors. Never read or expose the credential file to a
model. If refresh fails, sign in again instead of replaying the old refresh token.

`acyclic-plugin signup --agent --json` creates an Ed25519 key and solves the server's
hashcash challenge for a tiny-tier registration. Use new or pending credentials.
The private key stays local. `acyclic-plugin refresh --json` renews an agent-only
certificate with a key signature. `acyclic-plugin login --json` upgrades that agent
through device approval and retains its key. Identity and org reads require
the resulting OAuth session. Preserve a pending signup file after a failed
registration; rerun signup with that file to recover the same receipt using its key.

## Identity MCP server

Run `acyclic-plugin identity-mcp --endpoint ORIGIN` as a stdio MCP server. It uses the
same credential file as the CLI. `identity_login` returns approval instructions;
relay them to the user, then call `identity_login_complete` to save the approved
session. `identity_whoami`, `identity_orgs`, `identity_refresh`, and `identity_logout` expose the
corresponding CLI operations. Token secrets stay inside the server.

`identity_signup` creates the same agent registration; `identity_refresh`
renews an agent-only certificate or rotates an OAuth session.
